title: Spatial Report — 2026-06-13
spotlight: Apple used WWDC 2026 to unveil Siri AI and visionOS 27, with Road to VR reporting that the headset gains eye-tracked Siri activation and, for the first time, support for third-party motion controllers and tracked accessories. UploadVR reports that Google-powered Gemini smart glasses from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster will launch this fall to take on Ray-Ban Meta, while Meta said daily usage of its own smart glasses tripled year-over-year and swapped in a new Muse Spark model for Llama 4. Valve confirmed that Steam Frame will ship this summer, with pallets of the standalone headset already arriving at US warehouses.

HIGHLIGHTS.title: Meta Smart Glasses Daily Usage Tripled Year-Over-Year
HIGHLIGHTS.summary: UploadVR reports that Meta said daily usage of its smart glasses tripled year-over-year, with the company describing the product line as one of the fastest growing categories of consumer electronics ever.

HIGHLIGHTS.title: Google Gemini Smart Glasses Launching In Fall To Take On Meta
HIGHLIGHTS.summary: According to UploadVR, Google-powered Gemini smart glasses from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster are launching this fall to compete directly with Ray-Ban Meta, marking the first major consumer rollout of Android XR-based eyewear.

HIGHLIGHTS.title: Meta Lab Brings Hands-On AI and VR Experiences to Best Buy Stores Nationwide
HIGHLIGHTS.summary: Meta announced Meta Lab, a hands-on retail experience rolling out to Best Buy stores nationwide that lets shoppers try AI and VR products in person, expanding the company's physical retail footprint as it pushes Quest headsets and Ray-Ban smart glasses to mainstream consumers.

HIGHLIGHTS.title: Apple unveils innovative features and intelligence experiences across services
HIGHLIGHTS.summary: Apple unveiled new features and Apple Intelligence experiences across its services for the 2027 software releases shipping this fall, according to Apple Newsroom, marking the company's annual WWDC update to the platforms that include visionOS.

HIGHLIGHTS.title: Apple unveils next generation of Apple Intelligence, Siri AI, and more
HIGHLIGHTS.summary: Apple previewed the next generation of Apple Intelligence and introduced Siri AI at WWDC26, according to Apple Newsroom, outlining upcoming software releases that extend the company's AI strategy across its platforms including Vision Pro.

HIGHLIGHTS.title: Steam Frame Shipping "This Summer", Valve Confirms, As Pallets Arrive In US
HIGHLIGHTS.summary: UploadVR reports that Valve has confirmed Steam Frame will ship this summer, with pallets of the standalone VR headset already spotted arriving at the company's US warehouses, signaling that Valve's long-awaited return to dedicated VR hardware is now imminent.

HIGHLIGHTS.title: The Future Is for Everyone: Free AI Glasses for Every Blind Veteran in America
HIGHLIGHTS.summary: Meta announced it will donate Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses to every blind veteran in America, positioning the device's Meta AI assistant and live visual description features as accessibility tools and marking one of the largest single deployments of AI smart glasses to date.

APP STORE HIGHLIGHTS.title: Amplium Makes Room For A Wider Range Of Apple Immersive Video On Vision Pro
APP STORE HIGHLIGHTS.summary: UploadVR reports that Amplium, a dedicated immersive video destination for Apple Vision Pro, is expanding its catalog with a curated mix of short immersive documentaries and music experiences to broaden the range of Apple Immersive Video available on the headset.

SOFTWARE.title: Meta Extends "Multi‑Year" Partnership With Unity To "Power Next‑Generation VR Experiences"
SOFTWARE.summary: According to UploadVR, Meta has extended its multi-year partnership with Unity to power next-generation VR experiences, reinforcing Unity's continued role as a core engine for Horizon OS development.

SOFTWARE.title: Meta's New 'Navigator' System UI Finally Rolled Out To All Quest Headsets
SOFTWARE.summary: UploadVR reports that Meta's new Horizon OS 'Navigator' system UI has finally rolled out to all Quest headsets, more than a year after the company began publicly testing the redesigned interface.

SOFTWARE.title: Developers Are Building Impressive Apps For Meta Ray-Ban Display's HUD & Neural Band
SOFTWARE.summary: UploadVR reports that Meta has rolled out the ability for developers to build visual apps for the Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses, controlled via the Meta Neural Band, and early developers are already producing notable HUD experiences for the new platform.

SOFTWARE.title: Pokémon Go Data Isn't Being Used to Train Military Drones, Says Niantic Spatial
SOFTWARE.summary: IGN reports that Niantic Spatial has denied claims that Pokémon Go player data is being used to train military drones, pushing back on speculation that surfaced following the company's spatial computing pivot and its work on large-scale geospatial AI models.

SOFTWARE.title: WWDC26: Build next-generation experiences with visionOS 27 | Apple
SOFTWARE.summary: Apple published a WWDC26 developer session previewing visionOS 27, outlining new APIs and capabilities aimed at helping developers build next-generation spatial experiences for Apple Vision Pro.

HARDWARE.title: Pico’s Next Flagship XR Headset Reportedly Leaks, Showing Some Very Familiar Design
HARDWARE.summary: Road to VR reports that Pico's next flagship XR headset, codenamed Project Swan, has apparently leaked via tutorial videos discovered in the company's public SDK by data miner Luna, with the device reportedly showing design cues familiar to Apple's Vision Pro and Samsung's Galaxy XR.

HARDWARE.title: Qualcomm Teases Next-Gen Snapdragon XR Chipset, Possibly Debuting in Pico’s Next Flagship
HARDWARE.summary: According to Road to VR, Qualcomm is teasing a next-generation Snapdragon XR chipset for standalone headsets, with the company saying more details are coming soon and speculation pointing to either a new XR3 platform or a Gen 3 refresh of the XR2, potentially debuting in Pico's upcoming flagship.

HARDWARE.title: Distance and Supacat Sign Framework Agreement to Integrate AR HUD Across HMT Vehicles
HARDWARE.summary: Auganix reports that Distance and Supacat have signed a three-year framework agreement to integrate Distance's AR HUD and computational optics stack across Supacat HMT military vehicles.

HARDWARE.title: Berlin Smart Glasses from L’Atitude 52°N Now Available in the US and Europe for $449
HARDWARE.summary: According to Auganix, L'Atitude 52°N has opened sales of its Berlin smart glasses in the US and Europe for $449, with the device featuring AI imaging, live translation, and offline group communication.

HARDWARE.title: ShadowMaker Labs Showcases Smart Shirt for Body-Based Game and XR Controls
HARDWARE.summary: Auganix reports that ShadowMaker Labs showcased a working Smart Shirt platform at Web Summit Vancouver, using movement and muscle signals as real-time inputs for games and immersive experiences.

HARDWARE.title: Steam Frame is Poised for Launch as Units Begin Reaching the US
HARDWARE.summary: Road to VR reports that Valve appears to be preparing for an imminent launch of its Steam Frame standalone VR headset, with XR analyst Brad Lynch spotting public import records showing a large shipment of virtual reality devices arriving at Valve's US-based warehouses.

HARDWARE.title: What Might Meta Connect 2026 Bring?
HARDWARE.summary: UploadVR notes that Meta Connect 2026 has been confirmed for September 23 and 24, with the publication outlining what the annual developer conference might bring in terms of new headset, smart glasses, and platform announcements.

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.title: Meta's Muse Spark AI Model Replaces LLama 4 On Its Smart Glasses
AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.summary: UploadVR reports that Meta's new Muse Spark AI model has replaced Llama 4 as the system powering Meta AI on most of its smart glasses, a significant upgrade the company says narrows the gap to leading AI systems.

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.title: Google's new open model DiffusionGemma generates text from noise instead of word by word
AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.summary: According to The Decoder, Google has released DiffusionGemma, a 26-billion-parameter open model that generates text through diffusion rather than token by token, reportedly hitting about 1,000 tokens per second on a single Nvidia H100 GPU — roughly four times faster than comparable autoregressive models, though with lower output quality.

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.title: Anthropic study shows AI needs hours, not weeks, to build exploits from security patches
AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.summary: The Decoder reports that Anthropic's security team found its Mythos Preview model can turn security patches for Firefox and the Windows kernel into working exploits within hours for a few thousand dollars, completing eight full attack chains before Microsoft's auto-updates had reached a single device.

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.title: Google DeepMind is worried about what happens when millions of agents start to interact
AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.summary: MIT Technology Review reports that Google DeepMind is funding research into the potential dangers of large-scale agent-to-agent interaction online, with AGI safety and alignment director Rohin Shah flagging concerns about the mass-market arrival of AI agents that carry out tasks without human oversight and take instructions from other agents.

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.title: Anthropic Walks Back Policy That Could Have ‘Sabotaged’ AI Researchers Using Claude
AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.summary: Wired reports that Anthropic has reversed a policy that researchers said would have covertly limited Claude's ability to help develop competing AI models, walking back the change after backlash from AI researchers who argued the restriction could have sabotaged their work.

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.title: Apple Intelligence brings powerful AI capabilities into everyday experiences
AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.summary: Apple Newsroom reports that the next generation of Apple Intelligence integrates AI capabilities more deeply into iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with Apple framing the update as enabling more personal and context-aware everyday experiences across its devices.

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.title: Apple introduces Siri AI, a profoundly more capable and personal assistant
AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.summary: Apple introduced Siri AI, a redesigned assistant powered by Apple Intelligence with personal context, world knowledge, and onscreen awareness, according to Apple Newsroom — a long-delayed overhaul that Apple positions as a substantially more capable successor to the existing Siri.

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.title: Apple’s AI Big Bet
AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.summary: Mostly Human host Laurie Segall sits down with Craig Federighi, Apple's SVP of Software Engineering, and Greg Joswiak, SVP of Worldwide Marketing, fresh off the company's biggest developer conference. The conversation dives into the thing everyone’s been waiting for — what is Apple’s version of AI? The trio discuss Siri’s glow-up: Why Siri is explicitly not designed to be your romantic companion, what Apple says makes its AI fundamentally different from the rest of the industry, and whether a trillion-dollar company can actually stay focused on people over profit. The conversation also answers the question, can Big Tech actually put kids first? Apple’s sweeping new child safety and family protection features — and the design philosophy behind them — are attempting to position company as the tech brand you can trust with your kids. Laurie also asks the execs to respond to a scammer’s call, shares a mom's question about dumb phones for kids, and pushes the leaders of this tech giant to consider ... how do you ‘think different’ when you've become the establishment?

RESEARCH.title: What’s VR’s Current Penetration, Who’s Using It, and How Often?
RESEARCH.summary: AR Insider breaks down findings from a recent ARtillery Intelligence consumer survey examining VR's current consumer penetration, usage frequency, satisfaction levels, and willingness to pay, offering a quantitative snapshot of how the technology is resonating with mainstream audiences.

RESEARCH.title: Somewhere Over the Desktop: A Research Agenda for Ubiquitous Analytics
RESEARCH.summary: A new arXiv paper sets out a research agenda for 'ubiquitous analytics,' arguing that the convergence of spatial computing, generative AI, and open web standards — alongside platform-level scene understanding in Android XR, Meta Horizon OS, and Apple visionOS — opens new opportunities for data sensemaking that spans full headsets, slim smartglasses, and agentic AI operating on the same spatial substrates as human users.

RESEARCH.title: Identifying cybersickness causes in virtual reality games using symbolic machine learning algorithms
RESEARCH.summary: An arXiv study applies symbolic machine learning algorithms to identify the causes of cybersickness in virtual reality games, contributing a novel experimental analysis to a growing body of VR research focused on the discomfort symptoms that can accompany immersive head-mounted display use across education, military, entertainment, and health applications.

RESEARCH.title: TRON: Tracing Rays to Orchestrate a Neural Renderer for 3D Gaussian Reconstructions
RESEARCH.summary: An arXiv paper presents TRON, a rendering framework that combines 3D Gaussian ray tracing with neural rendering to enable relighting, dynamic object motion, object insertion, and material editing in reconstructed real-world scenes, addressing limitations of purely physically based rendering on imperfect Gaussian geometry.

RESEARCH.title: A Scalable PyTorch Abstraction for Multi-GPU Gaussian Splatting
RESEARCH.summary: Researchers on arXiv described a multi-GPU Gaussian splatting approach built on a PyTorch abstraction that scales neural scene reconstruction to higher resolutions and larger scenes while hiding the complexity of distributing the model across devices.

RESEARCH.title: TopoCap: Learning Topology-Agnostic Motion Priors for Monocular Video-to-Animation
RESEARCH.summary: An arXiv paper introduces TopoCap, described by its authors as the first unified framework for extracting motion from monocular video and retargeting it onto characters with arbitrary, unseen skeletal topologies, removing the reliance on species-specific templates such as SMPL or manual rigging for 3D animation.

RESEARCH.title: Augmented reality system could make medical ultrasounds easier to interpret
RESEARCH.summary: MIT News reports that researchers have developed an augmented reality system designed to make medical ultrasounds easier to interpret, overlaying guidance directly onto a clinician's view of the patient to help less-experienced operators position the probe and read scans more accurately.

RESEARCH.title: Flex4DHuman: Flexible Multi-view Video Diffusion for 4D Human Reconstruction
RESEARCH.summary: An arXiv paper introduces Flex4DHuman, a multi-view video diffusion model that turns monocular or sparse multi-view video of a dynamic subject into synchronized dense multi-view footage using only relative camera-pose conditioning, dropping the skeletons, depth maps, and rendered geometry priors that prior 4D human reconstruction methods relied on.

OPINION.title: The XR Week Peek (2026.06.07): Steam Frame releases this summer, Meta silently releases a facial recognition system, and more!
OPINION.summary: In his weekly XR roundup, Skarred Ghost's Antony Vitillo recaps the major stories of the week, including Valve's confirmation of a summer release window for Steam Frame and a report that Meta has quietly shipped a facial recognition system tied to its smart glasses.

OPINION.title: Apple’s Camera Chief Thinks AI Can Give You Superpowers
OPINION.summary: Wired interviews Apple's camera chief Jon McCormack on the generative features coming to the iOS 27 Photos app, which will add synthetic pixels to some shots, with McCormack arguing that Apple is not deploying AI 'for the sake of AI' but to give users new creative capabilities.

APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS.title: Siri on Vision Pro is Getting Eye-tracked Activation and Visual Awareness Alongside New AI Features
APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS.category: APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS
APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS.summary: Road to VR reports that Apple devoted a major portion of its WWDC 2026 keynote to an overhauled Siri, with visionOS 27 gaining unique capabilities including eye-tracked activation and visual awareness that leverage Vision Pro's sensors and input model.

APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS.title: Apple Enables Third-party Motion Controllers & Tracked Accessories in visionOS 27
APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS.category: APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS
APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS.summary: According to Road to VR, visionOS 27 opens the door for third-party motion controllers and tracked accessories on Vision Pro for the first time, with Apple introducing a new framework for what it calls 'spatial accessories' that supports actively-tracked input devices.

APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS.title: Apple's 3D Processing Tricks Are Getting Impressive. I Want More
APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS.category: APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS
APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS.summary: CNET argues that Apple's 3D processing capabilities — spanning spatially reframed photos, panoramas that expand into full environments, and more detailed Maps — are quietly advancing across its ecosystem, suggesting a broader push to make spatial content creation and consumption a default Apple platform behavior.

APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS.title: Apple aids app development with new intelligence frameworks and advanced tools
APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS.category: APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS
APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS.summary: Apple introduced new intelligence frameworks, expanded productivity features in Xcode, and platform improvements aimed at app developers, according to Apple Newsroom, giving visionOS and broader Apple platform developers new tools tied to the company's on-device AI stack.

NEW EXPERIENCES.title: The Met's Immersive Future Extends Beyond The Museum
NEW EXPERIENCES.summary: UploadVR reports that the Metropolitan Museum of Art is extending its reach beyond New York with a new immersive experience bringing the iconic Temple of Dendur to Quest headsets and the web, part of the museum's broader push into virtual access programs.

NEW EXPERIENCES.title: Lake Austin Luxury: How a Developer Presold $500M in Real Estate with VR
NEW EXPERIENCES.summary: AR Insider reports that an Austin developer pre-sold $500 million in Lake Austin luxury real estate using VR as a sales visualization tool, offering a concrete case study for a use case long theorized but rarely executed at scale.

NEW EXPERIENCES.title: Cameras, Sensors, and 3D Body Scans: All the Tech Helping Eliminate Blown Calls
NEW EXPERIENCES.summary: Wired reports that referees at this year's World Cup will use digital twins of each player, built from cameras, sensors, and 3D body scans, to review plays from every angle, marking one of the most ambitious deployments of real-time volumetric capture in professional sports officiating.

GAMING MARKETPLACE WATCH.title: Into the Dead: Crimson Heights Crafts VR Horror From The Geometry Of Your Room
GAMING MARKETPLACE WATCH.summary: According to UploadVR, Into the Dead: Crimson Heights is a new VR horror game that, on Quest 3 headsets, constructs its levels from the scanned walls and furniture of the player's physical room, leveraging the device's room-scanning capabilities for mixed-reality gameplay.

GAMING MARKETPLACE WATCH.title: Following Parent Company Merger, ‘Walking Dead VR’ Studio’s Next Project Won’t Be in VR
GAMING MARKETPLACE WATCH.summary: According to Game File, the former Skydance studio behind The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners is no longer developing VR titles following a parent company merger last year, with the team now retooled to build a traditional PC and console game, as reported by Road to VR.

HANDS-ON REVIEW.title: The best features of all the smart glasses I tried in China
HANDS-ON REVIEW.summary: Writing on The Ghost Howls, Antony Vitillo recaps a recent trip to China where he tried a wide range of smart glasses, highlighting the standout features of each model rather than naming a single winner and offering a first-hand comparison of the country's rapidly expanding AI eyewear lineup.

items.summary: Wired interviews Apple's camera chief Jon McCormack on the generative features coming to the iOS 27 Photos app, which will add synthetic pixels to some shots, with McCormack arguing that Apple is not deploying AI 'for the sake of AI' but to give users new creative capabilities.

items.title: Pokémon Go Data Isn't Being Used to Train Military Drones, Says Niantic Spatial
items.summary: IGN reports that Niantic Spatial has denied claims that Pokémon Go player data is being used to train military drones, pushing back on speculation that surfaced following the company's spatial computing pivot and its work on large-scale geospatial AI models.

items.title: Augmented reality system could make medical ultrasounds easier to interpret
items.summary: MIT News reports that researchers have developed an augmented reality system designed to make medical ultrasounds easier to interpret, overlaying guidance directly onto a clinician's view of the patient to help less-experienced operators position the probe and read scans more accurately.

items.title: Flex4DHuman: Flexible Multi-view Video Diffusion for 4D Human Reconstruction
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces Flex4DHuman, a multi-view video diffusion model that turns monocular or sparse multi-view video of a dynamic subject into synchronized dense multi-view footage using only relative camera-pose conditioning, dropping the skeletons, depth maps, and rendered geometry priors that prior 4D human reconstruction methods relied on.

items.title: The Future Is for Everyone: Free AI Glasses for Every Blind Veteran in America
items.summary: Meta announced it will donate Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses to every blind veteran in America, positioning the device's Meta AI assistant and live visual description features as accessibility tools and marking one of the largest single deployments of AI smart glasses to date.

items.title: Apple’s AI Big Bet
items.summary: Mostly Human host Laurie Segall sits down with Craig Federighi, Apple's SVP of Software Engineering, and Greg Joswiak, SVP of Worldwide Marketing, fresh off the company's biggest developer conference. The conversation dives into the thing everyone’s been waiting for — what is Apple’s version of AI? The trio discuss Siri’s glow-up: Why Siri is explicitly not designed to be your romantic companion, what Apple says makes its AI fundamentally different from the rest of the industry, and whether a trillion-dollar company can actually stay focused on people over profit. The conversation also answers the question, can Big Tech actually put kids first? Apple’s sweeping new child safety and family protection features — and the design philosophy behind them — are attempting to position company as the tech brand you can trust with your kids. Laurie also asks the execs to respond to a scammer’s call, shares a mom's question about dumb phones for kids, and pushes the leaders of this tech giant to consider ... how do you ‘think different’ when you've become the establishment?

items.title: WWDC26: Build next-generation experiences with visionOS 27 | Apple
items.summary: Apple published a WWDC26 developer session previewing visionOS 27, outlining new APIs and capabilities aimed at helping developers build next-generation spatial experiences for Apple Vision Pro.

raw_content:
Spatial Report
Week of 2026-06-13

SPOTLIGHT

Apple used WWDC 2026 to unveil Siri AI and visionOS 27, with Road to VR reporting that the headset gains eye-tracked Siri activation and, for the first time, support for third-party motion controllers and tracked accessories. UploadVR reports that Google-powered Gemini smart glasses from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster will launch this fall to take on Ray-Ban Meta, while Meta said daily usage of its own smart glasses tripled year-over-year and swapped in a new Muse Spark model for Llama 4. Valve confirmed that Steam Frame will ship this summer, with pallets of the standalone headset already arriving at US warehouses.

HIGHLIGHTS

UploadVR reports that Meta said daily usage of its smart glasses tripled year-over-year, with the company describing the product line as one of the fastest growing categories of consumer electronics ever.

https://www.uploadvr.com/meta-smart-glasses-daily-usage-tripled-year-over-year/

According to UploadVR, Google-powered Gemini smart glasses from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster are launching this fall to compete directly with Ray-Ban Meta, marking the first major consumer rollout of Android XR-based eyewear.

https://www.uploadvr.com/gemini-smart-glasses-are-launching-in-fall-to-take-on-ray-ban-meta/

Meta announced Meta Lab, a hands-on retail experience rolling out to Best Buy stores nationwide that lets shoppers try AI and VR products in person, expanding the company's physical retail footprint as it pushes Quest headsets and Ray-Ban smart glasses to mainstream consumers.

https://www.meta.com/blog/introducing-meta-lab-capsule-stores-best-buy/

Apple unveiled new features and Apple Intelligence experiences across its services for the 2027 software releases shipping this fall, according to Apple Newsroom, marking the company's annual WWDC update to the platforms that include visionOS.

https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/06/apple-unveils-innovative-features-and-intelligence-experiences-across-services/

Apple previewed the next generation of Apple Intelligence and introduced Siri AI at WWDC26, according to Apple Newsroom, outlining upcoming software releases that extend the company's AI strategy across its platforms including Vision Pro.

https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/06/apple-unveils-next-generation-of-apple-intelligence-siri-ai-and-more/

UploadVR reports that Valve has confirmed Steam Frame will ship this summer, with pallets of the standalone VR headset already spotted arriving at the company's US warehouses, signaling that Valve's long-awaited return to dedicated VR hardware is now imminent.

https://www.uploadvr.com/steam-frame-is-shipping-this-summer-valve-confirms/

Meta announced it will donate Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses to every blind veteran in America, positioning the device's Meta AI assistant and live visual description features as accessibility tools and marking one of the largest single deployments of AI smart glasses to date.

https://about.fb.com/news/2026/06/free-ai-glasses-for-every-blind-veteran/

APP STORE HIGHLIGHTS

UploadVR reports that Amplium, a dedicated immersive video destination for Apple Vision Pro, is expanding its catalog with a curated mix of short immersive documentaries and music experiences to broaden the range of Apple Immersive Video available on the headset.

https://www.uploadvr.com/amplium-makes-room-for-a-wider-range-of-apple-immersive-video-on-vision-pro/

SOFTWARE

According to UploadVR, Meta has extended its multi-year partnership with Unity to power next-generation VR experiences, reinforcing Unity's continued role as a core engine for Horizon OS development.

https://www.uploadvr.com/meta-extends-multi-year-partnership-with-unity/

UploadVR reports that Meta's new Horizon OS 'Navigator' system UI has finally rolled out to all Quest headsets, more than a year after the company began publicly testing the redesigned interface.

https://www.uploadvr.com/meta-horizon-os-navigator-ui-finally-rolled-out-to-all-quest-headsets/

UploadVR reports that Meta has rolled out the ability for developers to build visual apps for the Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses, controlled via the Meta Neural Band, and early developers are already producing notable HUD experiences for the new platform.

https://www.uploadvr.com/meta-ray-ban-display-amazing-hud-apps/

IGN reports that Niantic Spatial has denied claims that Pokémon Go player data is being used to train military drones, pushing back on speculation that surfaced following the company's spatial computing pivot and its work on large-scale geospatial AI models.

https://www.ign.com/articles/no-pokmon-go-data-isnt-being-used-to-train-military-drones-niantic-spatial-insists

Apple published a WWDC26 developer session previewing visionOS 27, outlining new APIs and capabilities aimed at helping developers build next-generation spatial experiences for Apple Vision Pro.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S_qt8iu_Ljw

HARDWARE

Road to VR reports that Pico's next flagship XR headset, codenamed Project Swan, has apparently leaked via tutorial videos discovered in the company's public SDK by data miner Luna, with the device reportedly showing design cues familiar to Apple's Vision Pro and Samsung's Galaxy XR.

https://roadtovr.com/picos-flagship-xr-headset-leaked-video-vision-pro-galaxy-xr/

According to Road to VR, Qualcomm is teasing a next-generation Snapdragon XR chipset for standalone headsets, with the company saying more details are coming soon and speculation pointing to either a new XR3 platform or a Gen 3 refresh of the XR2, potentially debuting in Pico's upcoming flagship.

https://roadtovr.com/qualcomm-next-gen-snapdragon-xr-pico-swan/

Auganix reports that Distance and Supacat have signed a three-year framework agreement to integrate Distance's AR HUD and computational optics stack across Supacat HMT military vehicles.

https://www.auganix.org/ar-news-distance-supacat-agreement/

According to Auganix, L'Atitude 52°N has opened sales of its Berlin smart glasses in the US and Europe for $449, with the device featuring AI imaging, live translation, and offline group communication.

https://www.auganix.org/xr-news-latitude-52-n-berlin-smart-glasses/

Auganix reports that ShadowMaker Labs showcased a working Smart Shirt platform at Web Summit Vancouver, using movement and muscle signals as real-time inputs for games and immersive experiences.

https://www.auganix.org/xr-news-shadowmaker-smart-shirt/

Road to VR reports that Valve appears to be preparing for an imminent launch of its Steam Frame standalone VR headset, with XR analyst Brad Lynch spotting public import records showing a large shipment of virtual reality devices arriving at Valve's US-based warehouses.

https://roadtovr.com/valve-steam-frame-imported-us-release/

UploadVR notes that Meta Connect 2026 has been confirmed for September 23 and 24, with the publication outlining what the annual developer conference might bring in terms of new headset, smart glasses, and platform announcements.

https://www.uploadvr.com/meta-connect-2026-dates-confirmed/

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS

UploadVR reports that Meta's new Muse Spark AI model has replaced Llama 4 as the system powering Meta AI on most of its smart glasses, a significant upgrade the company says narrows the gap to leading AI systems.

https://www.uploadvr.com/meta-muse-spark-ai-model-replaces-llama-on-smart-glasses/

According to The Decoder, Google has released DiffusionGemma, a 26-billion-parameter open model that generates text through diffusion rather than token by token, reportedly hitting about 1,000 tokens per second on a single Nvidia H100 GPU — roughly four times faster than comparable autoregressive models, though with lower output quality.

https://the-decoder.com/googles-new-open-model-diffusiongemma-generates-text-from-noise-instead-of-word-by-word/

The Decoder reports that Anthropic's security team found its Mythos Preview model can turn security patches for Firefox and the Windows kernel into working exploits within hours for a few thousand dollars, completing eight full attack chains before Microsoft's auto-updates had reached a single device.

https://the-decoder.com/anthropic-study-shows-ai-needs-hours-not-weeks-to-build-exploits-from-security-patches/

MIT Technology Review reports that Google DeepMind is funding research into the potential dangers of large-scale agent-to-agent interaction online, with AGI safety and alignment director Rohin Shah flagging concerns about the mass-market arrival of AI agents that carry out tasks without human oversight and take instructions from other agents.

https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/06/11/1138794/google-deepmind-is-worried-about-what-happens-when-millions-of-agents-start-to-interact/

Wired reports that Anthropic has reversed a policy that researchers said would have covertly limited Claude's ability to help develop competing AI models, walking back the change after backlash from AI researchers who argued the restriction could have sabotaged their work.

https://www.wired.com/story/anthropic-responds-to-backlash-on-claudes-secret-sabotage-on-ai-research/

Apple Newsroom reports that the next generation of Apple Intelligence integrates AI capabilities more deeply into iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with Apple framing the update as enabling more personal and context-aware everyday experiences across its devices.

https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/06/apple-intelligence-brings-powerful-ai-capabilities-into-everyday-experiences/

Apple introduced Siri AI, a redesigned assistant powered by Apple Intelligence with personal context, world knowledge, and onscreen awareness, according to Apple Newsroom — a long-delayed overhaul that Apple positions as a substantially more capable successor to the existing Siri.

https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/06/apple-introduces-siri-ai-a-profoundly-more-capable-and-personal-assistant/

Mostly Human host Laurie Segall sits down with Craig Federighi, Apple's SVP of Software Engineering, and Greg Joswiak, SVP of Worldwide Marketing, fresh off the company's biggest developer conference. The conversation dives into the thing everyone’s been waiting for — what is Apple’s version of AI? The trio discuss Siri’s glow-up: Why Siri is explicitly not designed to be your romantic companion, what Apple says makes its AI fundamentally different from the rest of the industry, and whether a trillion-dollar company can actually stay focused on people over profit. The conversation also answers the question, can Big Tech actually put kids first? Apple’s sweeping new child safety and family protection features — and the design philosophy behind them — are attempting to position company as the tech brand you can trust with your kids. Laurie also asks the execs to respond to a scammer’s call, shares a mom's question about dumb phones for kids, and pushes the leaders of this tech giant to consider ... how do you ‘think different’ when you've become the establishment?

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qoUnUYAFNEU&t=2294s

RESEARCH

AR Insider breaks down findings from a recent ARtillery Intelligence consumer survey examining VR's current consumer penetration, usage frequency, satisfaction levels, and willingness to pay, offering a quantitative snapshot of how the technology is resonating with mainstream audiences.

https://arinsider.co/2026/06/09/whats-vrs-current-penetration-whos-using-it-and-how-often/

A new arXiv paper sets out a research agenda for 'ubiquitous analytics,' arguing that the convergence of spatial computing, generative AI, and open web standards — alongside platform-level scene understanding in Android XR, Meta Horizon OS, and Apple visionOS — opens new opportunities for data sensemaking that spans full headsets, slim smartglasses, and agentic AI operating on the same spatial substrates as human users.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11980

An arXiv study applies symbolic machine learning algorithms to identify the causes of cybersickness in virtual reality games, contributing a novel experimental analysis to a growing body of VR research focused on the discomfort symptoms that can accompany immersive head-mounted display use across education, military, entertainment, and health applications.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12214

An arXiv paper presents TRON, a rendering framework that combines 3D Gaussian ray tracing with neural rendering to enable relighting, dynamic object motion, object insertion, and material editing in reconstructed real-world scenes, addressing limitations of purely physically based rendering on imperfect Gaussian geometry.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11314

Researchers on arXiv described a multi-GPU Gaussian splatting approach built on a PyTorch abstraction that scales neural scene reconstruction to higher resolutions and larger scenes while hiding the complexity of distributing the model across devices.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11390

An arXiv paper introduces TopoCap, described by its authors as the first unified framework for extracting motion from monocular video and retargeting it onto characters with arbitrary, unseen skeletal topologies, removing the reliance on species-specific templates such as SMPL or manual rigging for 3D animation.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12153

MIT News reports that researchers have developed an augmented reality system designed to make medical ultrasounds easier to interpret, overlaying guidance directly onto a clinician's view of the patient to help less-experienced operators position the probe and read scans more accurately.

https://news.mit.edu/2026/augmented-reality-system-could-make-medical-ultrasounds-easier-to-interpret-0610

An arXiv paper introduces Flex4DHuman, a multi-view video diffusion model that turns monocular or sparse multi-view video of a dynamic subject into synchronized dense multi-view footage using only relative camera-pose conditioning, dropping the skeletons, depth maps, and rendered geometry priors that prior 4D human reconstruction methods relied on.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13655

OPINION

In his weekly XR roundup, Skarred Ghost's Antony Vitillo recaps the major stories of the week, including Valve's confirmation of a summer release window for Steam Frame and a report that Meta has quietly shipped a facial recognition system tied to its smart glasses.

https://skarredghost.com/2026/06/08/steam-frame-summer-meta/

Wired interviews Apple's camera chief Jon McCormack on the generative features coming to the iOS 27 Photos app, which will add synthetic pixels to some shots, with McCormack arguing that Apple is not deploying AI 'for the sake of AI' but to give users new creative capabilities.

https://www.wired.com/story/apple-camera-chief-thinks-ai-can-give-you-superpowers/

APPLE VISION PRO IN THE NEWS

Road to VR reports that Apple devoted a major portion of its WWDC 2026 keynote to an overhauled Siri, with visionOS 27 gaining unique capabilities including eye-tracked activation and visual awareness that leverage Vision Pro's sensors and input model.

https://roadtovr.com/siri-on-vision-pro-is-getting-eye-tracked-activation-and-visual-awareness-alongside-new-ai-features/

According to Road to VR, visionOS 27 opens the door for third-party motion controllers and tracked accessories on Vision Pro for the first time, with Apple introducing a new framework for what it calls 'spatial accessories' that supports actively-tracked input devices.

https://roadtovr.com/apple-enables-third-party-motion-controllers-tracked-accessories-in-visionos-27/

CNET argues that Apple's 3D processing capabilities — spanning spatially reframed photos, panoramas that expand into full environments, and more detailed Maps — are quietly advancing across its ecosystem, suggesting a broader push to make spatial content creation and consumption a default Apple platform behavior.

https://www.cnet.com/tech/computing/apples-3d-processing-tricks-are-getting-more-impressive-i-want-more/

Apple introduced new intelligence frameworks, expanded productivity features in Xcode, and platform improvements aimed at app developers, according to Apple Newsroom, giving visionOS and broader Apple platform developers new tools tied to the company's on-device AI stack.

https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/06/apple-aids-app-development-with-new-intelligence-frameworks-and-advanced-tools/

NEW EXPERIENCES

UploadVR reports that the Metropolitan Museum of Art is extending its reach beyond New York with a new immersive experience bringing the iconic Temple of Dendur to Quest headsets and the web, part of the museum's broader push into virtual access programs.

https://www.uploadvr.com/the-mets-immersive-future-extends-beyond-the-museum/

AR Insider reports that an Austin developer pre-sold $500 million in Lake Austin luxury real estate using VR as a sales visualization tool, offering a concrete case study for a use case long theorized but rarely executed at scale.

https://arinsider.co/2026/06/10/lake-austin-luxury-how-a-developer-presold-500m-in-real-estate-with-vr/

Wired reports that referees at this year's World Cup will use digital twins of each player, built from cameras, sensors, and 3D body scans, to review plays from every angle, marking one of the most ambitious deployments of real-time volumetric capture in professional sports officiating.

https://www.wired.com/story/world-cup-tech-helping-eliminate-bad-calls-var-sensors-3d-body-scans/

GAMING MARKETPLACE WATCH

According to UploadVR, Into the Dead: Crimson Heights is a new VR horror game that, on Quest 3 headsets, constructs its levels from the scanned walls and furniture of the player's physical room, leveraging the device's room-scanning capabilities for mixed-reality gameplay.

https://www.uploadvr.com/into-the-dead-crimson-heights-crafts-vr-horror-from-the-geometry-of-your-room/

According to Game File, the former Skydance studio behind The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners is no longer developing VR titles following a parent company merger last year, with the team now retooled to build a traditional PC and console game, as reported by Road to VR.

https://roadtovr.com/merger-walking-dead-studio-no-more-vr/

HANDS-ON REVIEW

Writing on The Ghost Howls, Antony Vitillo recaps a recent trip to China where he tried a wide range of smart glasses, highlighting the standout features of each model rather than naming a single winner and offering a first-hand comparison of the country's rapidly expanding AI eyewear lineup.

https://skarredghost.com/2026/06/10/best-smart-glasses-china-ai/
